## Acceptance criteria

**AC1 - DIAGNOSE, and do not skip to a fix.** Establish by execution what happened to both emails.
Specifically: did the 2026-08-24 CV-Library email (19 roles) reach the pipeline at all, and why did
the 2026-08-25 email produce three rows with no title, no employer and no text? **Report the cause
with the evidence that proves it.** If the cause turns out to be something other than an extraction
bug - a collector that never ran, a parse that silently returned empty, a store that dropped the
text - say so plainly. **Larry has deliberately NOT written a cause into this order** because he has
been wrong doing that before.

**AC2 - the `content_verified` lie is in scope and may be the same defect.** An acquisition row
recording 11,917 characters read with `content_verified: true` while `original_text` is NULL is a
control asserting success for something that did not happen. Establish whether that is the same
root cause as AC1 or a second one. **A flag that can report verified without the content being
stored is worthless** - if that is what it does, say so.

**AC3 - failure must be LOUD.** Whatever the cause, the end state is that intake either captures the
advert or reports a specific visible failure naming what it could not extract. **Creating an empty
shell and moving on is the behaviour being removed.** Prove the loud path by making it fail on
purpose.

**AC4 - do not delete or rewrite the affected rows** (1401, 1402, 1404) or any historical row.
Recommend a disposition for them; Warwick decides. They are evidence until he says otherwise.

**AC5 - no live writes.** Diagnose against the live DB read-only and replay through fixtures. Your
`live_authority` permits reading and local runs only.
